title: Jeju tourism hit by safety concerns after mishandled missing person cases
summary: Jeju's reputation as a safe travel destination is coming under strain after police prematurely closed a missing person case and several missing people were later found dead. With domestic visitor numbers falling, concerns are growing over safety on the island. According to the Jeju Tourism Association on Sunday, domestic visitor numbers fell year-on-year on all but one day between Aug. 19 and Aug. 29. Aug. 19 was also when the police’s premature closure of the missing person case began drawing widespread public attention. title: Why president, chief justice are clashing over Supreme Court seat
summary: President Lee Jae Myung and Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, at odds for more than a year, are now locked in their most direct confrontation yet over the appointment of a Supreme Court justice. Cheong Wa Dae said Friday it would not submit to the National Assembly the confirmation motion for Sohn Bong-ki, a senior judge at the Daegu District Court nominated by Cho, and asked the chief justice to recommend another candidate. Senior presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said the powers to recommend and appoint justices are “assigned to different constitutional institutions,” arguing that Cho’s authority should respect the president’s substantive appointment power. title: Ticket scalping surges ahead of Seoul fireworks festival amid legal loophole
summary: Ticket scalping is once again rampant ahead of the Seoul International Fireworks Festival, with tickets being resold at steep markups just a week before the annual event at Yeouido Hangang Park. The government has moved to tighten laws against ticket scalping, but fireworks festivals fall outside the scope of existing regulations, leaving authorities with no legal grounds to crack down on resales and allowing the problem to persist year after year. The festival, now in its 22nd year, is scheduled to take place Saturday. The annual event draws around 1 million spectators each year. title: New jobs held by people in 20s, 30s decrease to record low in Q1
summary: The number of new jobs held by people in their 20s and 30s fell to a record low in the first quarter, government data showed Sunday. A combined 2.36 million new jobs were held by people in their 20s and 30s in the January-March period, down 23,000 from a year earlier, according to data from the Korean Statistical Information Service, an online portal operated by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The figure marked the lowest since the government began to compile such data in 2018. The number of new jobs held by people in their 20s fell by 26,000 to 1.34 million in the first quarter, also marking a record low. title: Lee nominates 6 ministers in Cabinet reshuffle
summary: President Lee Jae Myung reshuffled his Cabinet on Sunday, replacing ministers in six key posts as his administration faces mounting public criticism and falling approval ratings. Presidential chief of staff Kang Hoon-sik announced the nominations at a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae. Lee Hyoung-il, first vice minister of finance and economy, was tapped to serve as deputy prime minister for economic affairs and minister of finance and economy. Born in 1971, Lee is a veteran career bureaucrat who has held key posts since joining the finance ministry in 1993, building expertise in both domestic and international economics as a senior economist at the World Bank and as commissioner of Statistics Korea. title: Traffic, crime, fine dust top Seoul residents' smart city concerns: poll
summary: Seoul citizens named traffic congestion, nighttime crime and fine dust as the areas most in need of smart city solutions, a poll showed Sunday. The Korean megalopolis surveyed 8,531 Seoul residents online and offline from Feb. 10-21 last year as part of efforts to map out a smart city plan. Traffic, safety and the environment emerged as the three areas most in need of attention, cited by 37.5 percent, 21.2 percent and 16.2 percent of the respondents, respectively, according to the poll. When asked which areas most needed a smart city push specifically, the respondents again put traffic first at 30.1 percent, followed by safety at 27.5 percent and the environment at 18.8 percent. title: Fake office in Seoul helps reclusive youth fight social isolation
summary: In a quiet community center in western Seoul, 33 young adults recently committed to a novel daily routine: waking up, dressing and reporting for work at a company that exists entirely to help them reenter society. For many, stepping through the front door marked their tentative first foray into the outside world after months or even years spent largely behind closed bedroom doors. They are the newest employees at "NEET Company," a virtual firm operating in Seodaemun District through Oct. 19. Despite its corporate veneer, this office imposes no sales targets, demands no career milestones and measures no corporate performance metrics.
